title: Full Colour Print Wrap Vs. Colour Change Explained
description: Side-by-side comparison of full colour print wrap and solid colour change wrap on vehicles in the GTA

blocks.text: Full Colour Print vs. Colour Change Wrap: Understanding the Difference

blocks.html:
Full colour print wrap and colour change wraps are the two most popular paths to transforming a vehicle — but they are fundamentally different products, built for different goals. If you’re a business owner in Toronto weighing your options for a fleet, or a car enthusiast in Etobicoke considering a personal transformation, understanding exactly what sets these two wrap types apart could save you thousands of dollars and help you get results you’ll actually be happy with.

This guide breaks down both options in plain language: how each is made, how it looks, how long it lasts, how much it costs in Canada, and — most importantly — which one is right for your specific situation.

What Is a Full Colour Print Wrap?

A full colour print wrap is a digitally printed vinyl graphic applied to all of a vehicle’s exterior surface. The design — whether that’s your company logo, a photorealistic image, brand colours, contact information, or a fully custom illustration — is printed directly onto white cast vinyl using large-format inkjet printers. Once printed, the vinyl is laminated with a protective clear overlaminate to shield the ink from UV radiation, moisture, and road abrasion.

The key word here is custom. Full colour print wraps are built entirely from a digital file, meaning virtually any image, pattern, gradient, or graphic can be reproduced at large scale. For businesses across the GTA — from Mississauga logistics companies to Brampton contractors to Toronto food trucks — this is the go-to option for turning vehicles into mobile billboards.

What a full colour print wrap is used for:

  • Commercial fleet branding with logos, slogans, and contact details
  • Custom artistic or lifestyle graphics for personal vehicles
  • Food truck and retail vehicle branding
  • Promotional campaign wraps with time-sensitive messaging
  • Photorealistic imagery (e.g., product photos, landscape backgrounds)
  • Multi-colour gradients and full-panel illustrations

The base material for a quality print wrap is a cast vinyl such as 3M IJ180 or Avery Dennison MPI 1105. These films are specifically engineered for conformability around vehicle contours and are printed using UV-resistant inks. A protective overlaminate — typically a 2-mil gloss or matte cast film — is then applied on top. Without lamination, printed graphics will fade significantly faster.

Industry Note: According to 3M’s product specifications for their IJ180 series with Scotchcal 8518 overlaminate, properly laminated printed vehicle graphics are rated for up to five years of outdoor durability. Canadian wrap specialists using premium laminated cast vinyl routinely see graphics remain vibrant for five to seven years, depending on the vehicle’s exposure to Ontario’s freeze-thaw cycles, road salt, and UV load.

What Is a Colour Change Wrap?

A colour change wrap (also called a colour change car wrap or solid wrap) uses a pre-manufactured, pre-coloured cast vinyl film to alter a vehicle’s entire appearance — without any printing involved. Instead of a custom-designed graphic, you’re choosing from a curated library of solid colours, finishes, and textures that the vinyl manufacturer has built into the film itself.

Think of it like choosing a new paint colour — except the result is fully reversible, faster to apply, and often less expensive than a professional respray.

Premium colour change films like 3M 2080 series and Avery Dennison Supreme Wrapping Film come in an extraordinary range of finishes that paint simply cannot match:

  • Gloss (traditional high-shine look)
  • Matte (flat, paint-like finish)
  • Satin (between gloss and matte)
  • Metallic (shimmer and depth)
  • Chrome (mirror-finish)
  • Brushed metal (textured metallic appearance)
  • Colour-shift / flip (changes hue depending on viewing angle)
  • Textured (carbon fibre, leather-look, etc.)

Colour change wraps are ideal for personal vehicles — sports cars, luxury SUVs, daily drivers — where the owner wants a completely new aesthetic without the permanence of paint. They are also increasingly used on corporate vehicles to achieve a sleek, uniform fleet look.

Important distinction: Colour change wraps contain no printed graphics. They cannot display logos, text, gradients, or photographic imagery. For business vehicles that need branding, printed elements are typically added on top of a colour change base using cut vinyl or printed decals.

Side-by-Side Comparison

Cost Breakdown: What to Expect in the GTA

Pricing for both wrap types in Toronto, Etobicoke, Mississauga, Brampton, and Vaughan varies depending on vehicle size, panel coverage, design complexity, and vinyl brand.

Full Colour Print Wrap Pricing (Approximate CAD)

Prices include graphic design, printing, lamination, and professional installation. Costs may vary based on design complexity.

Colour Change Wrap Pricing (Approximate CAD)

Specialty finishes (chrome, colour-shift, premium Avery or 3M series) may add 10–30% to base pricing.

What drives the price difference?

Colour change wraps require more material per vehicle (since the entire surface must be covered with manufacturer-produced film, which costs more per square foot) and demand extremely precise installation — any imperfection, bubble, or lift is immediately visible on a solid surface. Printed wraps, by contrast, involve additional production steps (graphic design, RIP software, large-format printing, lamination) but allow more of the installation to happen off-vehicle.

Which Option Is Right for You?

The answer depends almost entirely on your goal.

Choose a Full Colour Print Wrap if you:

  • Own or manage a business and want your vehicles to generate leads while on the road
  • Need to display your logo, phone number, website, or service list
  • Want a completely custom artistic design (anime-inspired, camouflage, gradient, lifestyle graphic)
  • Are branding a food truck, retail vehicle, or event vehicle that needs maximum visual impact
  • Run a fleet in the GTA and want consistent commercial branding across all vehicles

Choose a Colour Change Wrap if you:

  • Want to completely transform the look of your personal vehicle without a permanent paint job
  • Are driving a leased vehicle and need a reversible solution (colour change wraps do not affect original paint, making them lease-friendly in most cases)
  • Want access to finishes unavailable through conventional automotive paint — matte, satin, colour-shift, chrome
  • Own a luxury or exotic vehicle and want to protect the factory paint while updating the colour
  • Are preparing to resell a vehicle and want to protect the original paint underneath

The Hybrid Approach

Many clients — especially businesses — combine both options. A tradesperson in Vaughan, for example, might wrap their truck in a solid 3M 2080 colour change film, then add printed decals with their company name, logo, and contact details. This hybrid approach gives them the clean, premium finish of a solid colour change wrap while still carrying a clear brand message.

At Vinyl Wrap Toronto, our in-house graphics design team can help you plan both elements from the start, so the design, colour palette, and layout all work together seamlessly.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

1. Confusing the two types when requesting quotes. If you ask for a “colour wrap” without specifying whether you want print or colour change, you may receive quotes for two different products at very different price points. Be specific about your goals — branding/graphics vs. colour change/aesthetic transformation.

2. Choosing a calendared vinyl for a printed wrap. Budget-tier calendared vinyl may look acceptable at first but lacks the conformability of cast vinyl. It will lift at edges and over complex body curves within 1–3 years, especially in Ontario’s extreme temperature range (from -30°C winters to +35°C summers). Always confirm your installer is using cast vinyl with a proper overlaminate for any printed wrap.

3. Skipping laminate on a printed wrap. Without lamination, UV exposure will fade printed graphics rapidly — sometimes within 12–18 months in a Canadian climate. A quality 2-mil overlaminate is non-negotiable for print work exposed to sunlight.

4. Expecting colour change film to display graphics. Colour change vinyl is a solid, pre-coloured film. It cannot reproduce logos, text, or imagery on its own. If you need any branding elements, those must be added separately as printed decals or cut vinyl lettering.

5. Underestimating preparation requirements. Neither wrap type performs well on paint that’s severely chipped, rusted, or contaminated. The vehicle surface must be clean, smooth, and free of contaminants before installation. A good wrap shop will assess your vehicle’s surface condition before quoting.

Material Spotlight: 3M and Avery Dennison

At Vinyl Wrap Toronto, we work exclusively with premium materials from 3M and Avery Dennison — two of the world’s most trusted names in automotive vinyl.

For full colour print wraps, we use 3M IJ180 and Avery MPI series cast films — both engineered for conformability over complex vehicle surfaces, with excellent adhesion and cleanability. Combined with a rated overlaminate, these materials provide years of vibrant, road-tested performance in Canadian conditions.

For colour change wraps, we stock the full 3M 2080 and Avery Dennison Supreme Wrapping Film libraries — featuring hundreds of colours and finishes, all backed by manufacturer warranties.

Every installation at Vinyl Wrap Toronto is backed by our 3-year warranty against peeling, bubbling, and fading.

FAQ: Full Colour Print Wrap vs. Colour Change Wrap

  1. Can I get a colour change wrap with my logo on it?

    A standard colour change vinyl film cannot print graphics — it’s a solid-colour film. However, we commonly add printed or cut-vinyl decals on top of a colour change wrap to include logos, contact information, or branding. This is a popular hybrid approach for business vehicles across Toronto and the GTA.

  2. Which wrap type lasts longer — printed or colour change?

    Both high-quality cast vinyl wraps (printed and colour change) have comparable lifespans of five to seven years when properly installed and maintained. The key factors are material quality (cast vs. calendared vinyl), laminate protection on printed wraps, and how the vehicle is stored and cared for. Ontario winters and road salt exposure make quality installation especially important.

  3. Is a full colour print wrap more expensive than a colour change?

    Not always. Colour change wraps can actually cost more per square foot because the pre-coloured film is more expensive and the installation is highly demanding (imperfections show clearly on solid surfaces). Printed wraps involve production costs (design, printing, lamination) but can be more cost-effective on smaller vehicles or partial coverage. Get a quote for both and compare based on your specific vehicle and goals.

  4. Can I wrap a leased vehicle with either type?

    Both wrap types can be safely applied to leased vehicles. Since vinyl wrap is fully removable and does not affect the original paint when properly installed and removed, most Ontario lease agreements permit wrapping. Always confirm with your dealership or leasing company first. We also recommend reviewing our post on wrapping leased vehicles in Ontario for more detail.

  5. How long does it take to install each type?

    A full colour change wrap on a standard car typically takes two to four business days for installation. Full colour print wraps require additional production time (design and printing) before installation begins, so total turnaround is usually three to five business days, depending on complexity. Commercial fleet projects or vehicles requiring panel disassembly may take longer.

  6. Can a full colour print wrap reproduce my exact brand colours (Pantone)?

    Yes. Our team uses professional RIP software and colour management workflows calibrated to produce accurate Pantone-matched output. We recommend providing your brand’s Pantone Coated reference numbers for the most accurate colour reproduction. Proof prints are reviewed before full production.

  7. Will a colour change wrap protect my original paint?

    Yes — one of the primary benefits of any quality vinyl wrap, including colour change wraps, is paint protection. The vinyl shields the original factory paint from UV fading, minor stone chips, light scratches, and road grime. When removed professionally, the original paint is preserved underneath. This is especially valuable for maintaining resale value on luxury and exotic vehicles in the GTA.
